stages.reference: Make a close study of the tiny optical imperfections inside the companion smoke-brown stained glass. The warm amber-umber body comes from its existing base; this detail layer contributes uneven cooling, extremely faint flow lines, isolated small bubbles and a trace of mellow age. These marks should look embedded in translucent material, never engraved, highlighted or painted on its surface. Where light passes through the glass, brown pigmentation may shift gently with thickness but remain recognizably the same batch. Keep the design spare and physically plausible. Avoid decorative woodgrain, shining amber gemstones, mosaic boundaries, harsh brown stripes, scratches everywhere, thick fractures or a newly invented solid backdrop. The principal glass must remain the dominant visual material.
